items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: Arthur Durny, Larry Cartrell and myself, there were three weeks, when we left New Orleans. And who was on third? Durny. He was playing the piano.

ctx.x: Most of them do, but we had another one, like Hall, that didn't use the piano, he didn't know anything about the piano. But Billy Douglas, he said, I'm writing the whole arrangement out of his head, and touch any instrument. What about the... Yeah, it is. You can continue. Did you have any trouble with transposition or anything?

No. I mean, for the various instruments, because they would be in different keys. Yes. At first I had a little problem, but after it, it was just no problem. I see, because, yeah. Yeah. Things do make a difference that way. Yes. So, with... Who was the Reed section when you first came to the piano? And who was on third? Durny. He was playing the piano.
Yeah. Yeah. I mean, for the various instruments, because they would be in different keys. Yes.
